items.author: AK47angie
items.text:
This @Ferrari F40 was neither filmed nor generated by a video model: it was built entirely in code. @claudeai Fable 5.2 wrote every part in Python and @Blender 5.2 rendered it, with no downloaded models or textures. Music and sound design are by @higgsfield_ai.

931 real parts, each with a name, technical label and assembly order: tubular chassis, twin-turbo V8, transaxle, suspension, wheels, cabin, wiring and bodywork.
9,302 fasteners: rivets, bolts and nuts.
852 images rendered one by one, at 24 per second, for 35.5 seconds of film.
3 digital clay bodies, checked against period drawings and Ferrari's official dimensions before one was chosen.
The process was a workshop's: silhouette first, then the insides, then materials and studio light, and finally the animation, where each part flies in and locks into place while a single camera travels through the car. The body starts as glass, revealing the mechanics, and a wave turns it into Rosso Corsa.

The F40 (1987) marked Ferrari's 40th anniversary and was the last car approved by Enzo Ferrari. With no electronic aids, a Kevlar and carbon-fibre body, 478 hp and 324 km/h, it is the definitive analogue supercar. Today, almost 40 years after its debut, it remains one of the most iconic Ferraris ever made.

items.author: 0xCodio
items.text:
Fable 5.2 lays out a landscape by deciding where nobody would ever build

Terrain gets generated first and roads get drawn on top, which is why game maps have villages in places no one would have settled.

Nothing is placed by hand, the layout is written as code that reads the ground and scores every square metre for whether people could live on it:

> Score: slope, drainage, sun and distance to water
> Reject: everything that floods, slides or freezes
> Place: what remains gets roads, fields and houses

• What the habitability pass changes
> Villages sit on the dry side of the slope
> Fields take the flat ground, houses take the edge
> Roads follow the contour instead of cutting it

• Why decorated terrain reads as empty
> Buildings land where the artist had room
> Nothing in the map says why anyone stayed
> A settlement with no reason is a prop

A full map gets scored and settled in about six minutes.

And the part that broke my brain:

The hand placed village looked better in a screenshot and made no sense on foot.

The scored one put everything on one hillside, because that was the only ground worth having.

Same map. One version was arranged, the other was chosen.

The hard part was never filling the landscape.

It was working out where the land allows anything ↓

items.text:
This is getting out of hand: Claude Fable 5.2 can now take any gadget apart from one picture and nobody is talking about it.

I gave it one picture of a PS5 controller and got back one that splits open part by part in 24 seconds.

What made it work is teardown, a free open-source skill for Claude Code (3,000+ stars on GitHub) that makes Claude build the inside first.

Why model a controller by hand for a week when Claude can write every part as code?

Here is the workflow: from that one picture Claude writes the motion as math before it draws a single part, so every panel reads the same numbers as the model. It renders a still at every beat and fixes what it finds, then records the tour at 60 fps: the touchpad lifts, both sticks come out on their gimbals, the motor and gears behind L2 and R2 slide out and trigger force jumps from 30% to 78% the second push-back switches on.

Step-by-step setup:

1. Install teardown with one npx line
2. Open Claude Code and type /teardown
3. Give it one picture of the thing you want to see inside
4. Let it check every still before it films
5. Record the tour and watch it come apart

It runs inside Claude Code, so you'll never keyframe a teardown by hand again.

The full guide and every prompt are in the article below.

items.prompt:
幫我做一支 90 年代電視廣告風格的動畫短片，輸出成 mp4。

【做法限制】
- 每一格畫面都用程式畫（Python + Pillow），再用 ffmpeg 串成影片。
- 不要用任何 AI 生圖、生影片模型，也不要下載外部圖片、音效、音樂素材。
- 角色跟品牌都要原創，不要用現有的角色、吉祥物、真實品牌。

【內容】
- 主角：〔例：一隻愛睡覺的垂耳兔，米白色，圓滾滾〕
- 賣的東西（虛構）：〔例：兔子形狀的棉花糖〕
- 品牌名：〔例：好好吃布丁ㄏㄏㄏㄏ〕
- 標語：〔例：睡前來一顆！〕
- 長度：〔15／30／60〕秒
- 畫面上的文字用〔繁體中文／注音／英文〕

【劇情結構】
1. 開場：平淡或有點慘的日常，顏色偏暗、動作慢，畫面角落打上時間字卡。
2. 轉折：商品登場，畫面閃白，顏色整個變鮮豔。
3. 高潮：主角跟著節拍又跳又轉，背景一直換，大字一個一個彈出來。
4. 結尾：商品特寫＋品牌 logo＋標語＋「新上市」爆炸貼紙，最下面一行很小的免責聲明（寫好笑一點）。
先給我看分鏡表（每一段幾秒、畫面、文字、聲音），我確認之後再開始畫。

【畫風】
- 賽璐珞手繪感：粗的深色外框線、平塗色塊、不要漸層。
- 外框線要微微抖動，每 2 格重新抖一次；動畫用每秒 12 格。
- 動作要有擠壓和拉長（落地變扁、跳起來變長）；文字出現時先放大過頭再彈回來。
- 配色用高彩度的桃紅、黃、青綠、紫。
- 背景用旋轉的放射線、往外擴散的同心圓、飄來飄去的幾何小圖形（三角形、圓環、鋸齒線）。
- 字要粗、有外框、有錯位的彩色陰影。

【舊電視質感】（每一格畫完之後再套）
- 4:3 比例，先用 480x360 畫，最後放大到 640x480。
- 顏色往右暈開、亮度有細雜訊、每一列畫面左右微微錯位、最底下有幾列歪掉的雜訊帶。
- 偶爾有白色橫向刮痕；切換場景的那兩格雜訊要特別重。
- 掃描線、四角變暗、畫面邊緣微微往外凸、四個角是圓的。

【聲音】
- 全部用程式合成：方波的廣告歌（120 拍）、鼓、每個動作對應的音效。
- 套上錄音帶質感：音高微微飄、高頻削掉、有底噪。

【檢查方式】
- 先不要算整支影片。每個場景挑 2～3 個時間點畫出來，拼成一張總覽圖，打開來看，檢查文字有沒有超出畫面、角色有沒有畫歪、字讀不讀得清楚，改到沒問題再算整支。
- 整支算完後，從 mp4 裡抽幾格出來再看一次，並確認每一段都有聲音。
- 最後告訴我哪些確認過、哪些沒辦法確認。

items.prompt:
In Blender 5.2.3, using Python only (no downloaded assets, no add-ons, procedural materials only), build a 1960s-style rangefinder film camera as a hero product shot on a small desk vignette.

Camera: chrome top and bottom plates, black leatherette body with a visible grain texture, lens barrel with a knurled focus ring and an engraved distance scale with readable numbers, a working 8-blade aperture, a shutter speed dial with readable numbers, a film advance lever, rangefinder and viewfinder windows with glass, strap lugs. Real-world proportions, bevels on every hard edge. Spend your effort on details that read on screen at 1080p, not on tiny hidden parts.

Scene: dark walnut desk with procedural wood grain. The camera sits on a small round leather pad. Static props near the edges: a leather camera case with stitching, two 35mm film canisters, a lens cap, a small desk lamp with a warm glow. Dark far background with out-of-focus warm bokeh lights. Shallow depth of field.

Lighting: warm lamp key, cool rim light on the chrome, plus bright emissive softbox panels placed so the chrome has something to reflect. No environment texture.

Animation, 240 frames at 24 fps, fixed 50mm render camera, the film camera fills about 70% of the frame from frame 1:
1-120: the camera rotates 180 degrees on its pad.
120-180: the aperture closes from f/2 to f/16, clearly visible from the front.
180-240: exploded view. The camera separates into at least 12 named parts (top plate, bottom plate, body, lens barrel, focus ring, aperture blades, shutter dial, advance lever, viewfinder glass and so on) that slide apart along their axes above the desk and hold. Props stay put.

Render: Cycles, GPU OptiX, 1920x1080, 128 samples adaptive, OptiX denoise, PNG sequence to ./render, save the .blend.

Work autonomously and do not ask questions. Render test frames 1, 120 and 240 first and fix anything that is broken. Then start the full render in the background with the blender command line, tell me the exact command and stop. Do not wait for or poll the render.
